terms.meaning: A tool that records the history of files in a project folder.
A project folder tracked by git.
A file that lists what was published, so the site knows what to show.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup, imports and sample code
sections.what: Loads the modules the tests need and sets git author details. It also stores two sample source files used to build the fake repositories.
sections.why: Fixed author details make the fake commits repeatable.
sections.watch_out: The tests run real git commands, so git must be installed for them to pass.

sections.name: add
sections.title: Sample addition function
sections.what: A small function in the first sample file that adds two numbers.
sections.why: Gives the refresh routine a real function to write notes for.
sections.watch_out: The tests look for the names add and double, so renaming them breaks the expected results.

sections.name: double
sections.title: Sample doubling function
sections.what: A small function in the first sample file that doubles a number. A later test edits only this function.
sections.why: Lets a test prove that only the edited function needs a new note.
sections.watch_out: The change test replaces this exact text, so editing it breaks that test.

sections.name: git
sections.title: Helper that runs a git command
sections.what: Runs a git command inside a chosen folder and stops the test with an error if git fails.
sections.why: Lets tests create and change fake repositories.

sections.name: Refresh (part 1)
sections.title: Building fake portfolio and repositories
sections.what: For each test, creates a fake portfolio site and two fake repositories, Alpha (public) and Beta (private). It copies the tool into the site and provides helpers that run refresh and answer its questions with fake answers.
sections.why: Each test needs a clean setup with one public and one private repository.
sections.watch_out: The visibility and exclude settings in the test config decide what is published, so changing them changes every test result.

sections.name: Refresh: full_run
sections.title: Refresh end-to-end tests
sections.what: Runs a full refresh and checks that the public repository is published in full while the private one is kept to notes. It also checks that a small change needs one new note even from a fresh clone, that the budget stops the run, and that a secret keeps a repository to notes only.
sections.why: These checks cover the rules that protect private code and control cost.
sections.watch_out: The fresh clone test deletes the docs folder to imitate a clean checkout, so it depends on where local notes are kept.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Test runner start
sections.what: When the file is run directly, runs all tests and prints each result in detail.
sections.why: A standard way to start Python test files.

summary: Self-test for the refresh routine. It builds a fake portfolio and two fake repositories, then checks publishing, change detection, budget limits and secret handling.
purpose: Confirms refresh.py publishes only public code, reuses notes after small changes, stops at its budget, and holds back code that contains secrets.
why: The header states the aim: the tests protect private code and keep the routine's cost predictable.
how: Each test creates a temporary site and two git repositories, copies the tool into the site, runs the refresh steps in order, answers its questions with fake answers, and then checks the manifest and the saved notes.
inputs: Sample code and config values stored in this file, plus the tool files copied from tools/clarity.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test, printed by unittest.
risks: The tests run real git commands in temporary folders. If git is missing or misconfigured, every test fails at setup.
debug: Run the file with python3 and read the failing test's message. Many failures at once usually point to git setup. Check the output printed by the refresh command for the exact error.
